# swarm-ai — information for language models and tooling

Canonical repository: https://github.com/ellmos-ai/swarm_ai

`pyproject.toml` declares source version `0.1.3`. This declaration does not itself mean that a package has been published.

## What the project contains

swarm-ai is a Python toolkit with CLI entry points and examples for multi-agent coordination:

- Parallel chunk processing: `tools/translate_swarm.py`, `tools/summarize_chunks.py`
- Majority voting and result aggregation: `tools/consensus_swarm.py`
- Local SQLite marker storage: `tools/stigmergy_api.py`, `tools/stigmergy_init.py`
- Claude CLI and optional provider integration: `tools/runner.py`
- JSON-based hierarchy and specialist routing examples under `tools/`

These are libraries and examples, not a hosted agent service or production reliability guarantee.

## Data flow and limits

- SQLite coordination state is stored locally. Calls to Anthropic, Claude CLI, COMA-connected providers, or other configured services can send prompts and request data externally.
- `confidence` in consensus results is the winner count divided by all returned results, including failed results. `agreement_ratio` is calculated over valid answers. These values are not calibrated probabilities; a majority does not establish factual correctness.
- Team-lock claims are cooperative file-based coordination signals. Processes that ignore or edit the protocol can bypass them.
- Consensus, translation, and summarization require positive finite estimated-cost caps. `ClaudeRunner` has an optional cap; no single universal cap applies to every provider or workflow.
- The application runs with the caller's environment and permissions. `RunAsInvoker` is not an OS sandbox and does not guarantee non-elevation.
- The translation tool supports target text languages `de`, `en`, `es`, `zh`, `ja`, and `ru`. These are translation targets, not six localized UI languages. CLI help mixes English and German; the experimental Tk GUI has German labels.

## Useful files

- `README.md` and `README_de.md`: project overview and usage examples
- `SECURITY.md`: data flow, execution limits, and private vulnerability-reporting channels
- `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`: selected declared dependencies; not a transitive dependency audit
- `TODO.md`: current open tasks under `## Offene Aufgaben`
- `CHANGELOG.md`: historical changes; older statements may be superseded by later clarification
- `PYPI_RELEASE.md`: packaging and release checklist
- `results/benchmark_20260306.json`: one historical benchmark run; not a general performance claim
- `results/benchmark_20260813.json`: a dry-run record for the benchmark catalog

## Verification

CI configuration covers Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS with Python 3.10–3.13. Consult the current repository workflow for live results; this file does not publish a static test count or audit status. The repository's `LICENSE` is MIT. Third-party components have separate terms and notices.

## Related projects

- [COMA](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/coma): optional Spawner/adapter provider bridge used by Swarm when the `providers` extra is installed.
- [Roshambo](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/roshambo): separate toolkit for coordinating independently launched agents through serializable leases and outcome memory.
- [MarbleRun](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/marblerun): separate toolkit for configuring multi-agent chains.
